as_told.title: Immaculate Constellation report: triangle ARVs over Indo-PACOM

plain: Slowly rotating triangle-shaped craft are said to have appeared over INDOPACOM, the US military's Pacific command, according to the online researcher UAPGerb, who reads it in a report called Immaculate Constellation and in one telling calls them "adversarial" alien reproduction vehicles, meaning craft built by copying alien ones, seen over "Chinese territory" as triangles with three lights. The report itself is unsigned: the journalist Michael Shellenberger delivered it to Congress, Representative Nancy Mace entered it into the record of a House Oversight hearing on 13 November 2024 as a Pentagon document, a former Defense Department official named Matthew Brown later said he wrote it, and a Defense Department spokesperson said there is no record of a program by that name. The report describes a slowly rotating equilateral triangle over "a grouping of vessels engaged in SIGINT and MASINT collection", that is, ships gathering electronic intelligence at night in the Pacific Ocean, which expected it "due to foreign pre-positioning of advanced collection assets", and another triangle called "an ARV/RV of unknown origin". So the report does call the collection assets foreign, but it places the ships in the Pacific rather than over Chinese territory and gives the second craft's origin as unknown, which leaves UAPGerb's reading of an adversary's craft a step beyond its words.

discussion.by: Immaculate Constellation report (anonymous, entered into the House Oversight hearing record, 13 November 2024)
discussion.text: An unsigned report that Michael Shellenberger delivered to Congress and Rep. Nancy Mace entered into the record of the House Oversight hearing of 13 November 2024 as a document from the Pentagon; it calls itself the public version of a Defense Department employee's report, cleared for release by the State Department; Matthew Brown, a former Defense Department official, later said he wrote it; and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of a program by that name. The report has two triangle cases under INDOPACOM: in one a slowly rotating equilateral triangle appears over "a grouping of vessels engaged in SIGINT and MASINT collection at night in a specific area of the Pacific Ocean", and the vessels are said to have expected it "due to foreign pre-positioning of advanced collection assets"; in the other the triangle is "an ARV/RV of unknown origin". UAPGerb's "Chinese territory" and "adversarial ARV" are his reading of these cases, a step from their words: the first places the ships in the Pacific and calls the collection assets foreign, and the second gives the craft's origin as unknown.
